# StreamDek Mobile v2.1.13

*Version code 71*

## What's New

**StreamDek speaks your language**
StreamDek is now available in English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch and
Polish. Hindi coming soon. Choose one under **Settings › Appearance and Language › Language**, 
or leave it on **System Default** to follow the language your phone is already set to.

The change takes effect immediately. There is no restart, no sign-out and no reload — the screen you
are on simply changes language in place, keeping your scroll position and anything you had open. The
choice is remembered across restarts, reboots and app updates.

Languages are listed by their own names — Français, Deutsch, Español, Italiano, Português,
Nederlands, Polski — so a language chosen by accident is still easy to find your way back from. Your
language is set per device: choosing German on your phone leaves your television as it was.

**Artwork and descriptions in your language too**
StreamDek now asks its metadata sources for information in your chosen language, falling back to
English and then to the provider's default when a title has not been translated. Media pages never
come back empty because of it.

**TheIntroDB joins IntroDB as a timing provider**
Intro, recap, credits and outro timestamps — the data behind Skip Intro, Skip Recap and starting the
next episode — can now come from either **IntroDB** or **TheIntroDB**. Pick which one StreamDek asks
first under **Settings › Playback**, and add your key for it under **Content Services**, where a
guided setup walks you through where to get one, checks the key before saving it, and tells you
plainly if it was not accepted.

Leave **Automatically use the other provider when needed** on and StreamDek quietly falls back to
the second service whenever your preferred one has no usable timing for what you are watching. Two
sources cover far more than one, and the fallback is silent — you see skip controls appear, not a
provider being switched.

**Recommendations as a title finishes**
StreamDek can now suggest what to watch next as you approach the end of something, without
interrupting it. Choose how early the invitation appears — **Early**, **Standard** or **Late** — and
whether you see one suggestion or two. Turn the whole thing off if you would rather the credits just
run.

**A choice of episode layouts**
Series pages now offer two ways through a season. **Horizontal strip** keeps the familiar row of
wide cards you swipe along. **Vertical stack** lists the whole season down the page instead, one
episode per row, in a single continuous scroll — no paging, which suits a long season far better
than repeatedly swiping. Seasons can also be presented as regular tabs or as poster image tabs.

**Card captions on your terms**
Choose what appears beneath ordinary Home cards: **Show Full** for the title and year, **Show Year
Only** when the artwork already carries the title, or **Off** for a clean grid of posters.

## Improvements

**Everything reads in one language, not two**
Interface text across the app now follows your choice: Home rows, Search and its filters, title and
episode pages, the player and all of its panels, every Settings page, and the messages StreamDek
shows after an action. Counts, dates, times and decimals are written the way your language writes
them — "1,5x" rather than "1.5x" in German, and dates in each language's own order.

Titles, cast names, add-on and provider names, playlist names and stream descriptions are left
exactly as their source sent them. Those belong to the content, not to StreamDek.

**Room for longer words**
Page headings now scroll gently when a translation runs longer than the space available, instead of
squeezing the controls beside them. Player panel headings do the same, so a heading like
"Wiedergabegeschwindigkeit" no longer crushes the Close button.

**Add-on switches respond to the tap, not the network**
Turning an add-on on or off now moves the switch immediately and does the work behind it. It used to
sit unchanged for the whole round trip, and the refresh that followed re-fetched every installed
manifest before showing the result — which could turn an ordinary network delay into six to ten
seconds of an app that looked frozen. Rapid taps now settle on the last one you made, and switching
profile mid-request no longer lets an old reply overwrite the new profile's state.

**A quieter Playlists and Add-ons list**
Item cards on the Playlists and Add-ons settings pages have lost their outlines. The card's own
background already separates it from the page, and dropping the extra edge leaves the Add button as
the one outlined thing on the screen.

**A canonical API path, and a device identity on every request**
The app now talks to the backend through the canonical `/api/v1` prefix, and every request carries
this device's identity. Older bare paths continue to work, so nothing changes for you — but requests
are now attributable to a device, which is what makes linked-TV handoff and per-device sign-out
behave predictably.

## Fixed

**Password reset now requires the emailed code**
The reset flow could previously set a new password from an email address alone, because the
deployment had no mail server to deliver a code with. Knowing an address was enough to take the
account. That path is gone: StreamDek now emails you a code, tells you it expires in fifteen
minutes, and signs you in once you have spent it.

**Other fixes**

* Fixed a suspended account being left with the interface on screen and every request silently
  refused, which read as the app being broken rather than the account being stopped. A suspension
  now ends the session cleanly and says why on the sign-in screen.
* Fixed movies carrying stray provider season or episode metadata resuming as though they were
  series episodes.
* Fixed several settings showing English option names — Home card text, background modes, theme
  names, player control layouts and subtitle sources — while the rest of the page was translated.
* Fixed every inner Settings page keeping an English heading and description.
* Fixed the navigation bar, the subtitle panel tabs and the Continue Watching and Watchlist filters
  drawing internal names instead of translated labels.
* Fixed playback speeds and other numbers following the phone's system language rather than the
  language chosen for StreamDek.
* Fixed episode air dates showing in a fixed English format.
* Fixed seasons and untitled episodes being labelled in English even when the rest of the page was
  not.
* Fixed the player's Stream Info panel naming the delivery method and provider label in English.
* Fixed Settings search matching only English wording, so a page can now be found by typing what is
  actually on the screen.
